topStories.headline: Election Day Is Tuesday: School Board, City Council, and a 1% Sales Tax Referendum All on the Ballot
topStories.dek: Staunton voters head to the polls November 3 to fill three school board seats, three city council seats, and decide whether to approve a new local sales tax dedicated entirely to school construction.
topStories.body:
Staunton's November 3 general election carries unusually high stakes for a local ballot. In addition to federal races for U.S. Senate and House, residents will choose three members of the City School Board, three City Council members, and vote yes or no on a local referendum that could reshape how the school system pays for capital projects for the next two decades.

The school board race has five candidates competing for three at-large seats: incumbents Fontella Brown-Bundy and Kristin Siegel, plus challengers Cecilia Carpenter, Barbara White, and Jordan Zipser. On the council side, incumbents Brad Arrowood and Alice Woods are joined by challenger Billy Vaughn for three open seats.

The headline question on the ballot asks whether Staunton should be allowed to levy an additional local retail sales tax of up to 1%, with proceeds dedicated solely to the construction or major renovation of public school facilities. The tax would expire no later than July 23, 2046. If approved by voters, the City Council would still need to adopt an ordinance to put the levy into effect. City finance staff have estimated the tax could generate roughly $5.1 million to $5.4 million per year after exemptions for groceries and personal hygiene items — money that would go toward addressing what officials have described as $168 million in deferred school facility needs.

Early voting has been available at City Hall since September 22. A final early-voting opportunity runs Saturday, October 31, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. at City Hall, 116 W. Beverley Street. On Election Day itself, polls open at 6 a.m. and close at 7 p.m.; voters must report to their assigned precinct, not City Hall.

topStories.headline: City Holds Final Listening Session This Weekend on Future of Booker T. Washington Community Center
topStories.dek: Residents have one last chance to weigh in on what should become of the historic West End landmark before consultants compile their findings for City Council.
topStories.body:
The second and final public listening session on the future of Booker T. Washington Community Center takes place this Saturday, October 31, from 10 a.m. to noon at the center itself, 1114 W. Johnson Street. The City of Staunton is partnering with Richmond consulting firm The Spark Mill to facilitate the conversation, which is part of a broader community engagement process launched by City Manager Leslie Beauregard at the September 10 City Council meeting.

The building at the top of the steep West End hill has a long history. Originally built in 1936 as an Art Deco high school designed by architect Raymond V. Long, it served as the only high school for African-American students in the Staunton area for thirty years. The city formally repurposed it as a community center in 2001, and in 2014 it was listed on both the Virginia Landmarks Register and the National Register of Historic Places.

Revitalization of the center is a stated strategic goal in City Council's current Staunton Plan, and it was also a key recommendation in the adopted West End Revitalization Plan. Past community discussions have centered on expanding the building's offerings beyond its current gym, kitchen, and basketball courts to create a more complete neighborhood resource hub. The Spark Mill's engagement process also includes six to eight focused stakeholder interviews and a historical and demographic analysis, with a preliminary findings report due to council within six weeks of the process's conclusion.

Residents who cannot attend Saturday's session can submit comments through an online survey linked from the city's newsroom page at ci.staunton.va.us.

topStories.headline: The Well Balanced Paw Moves Into Bigger Downtown Space After Six Years
topStories.dek: The pet nutrition and wellness shop reopened Saturday at a new downtown address, giving owner Heather Leonard more room for services, events, and — for the first time — its own parking lot.
topStories.body:
After six years in its original downtown Staunton location, The Well Balanced Paw officially reopened on Saturday, October 24, in a larger space that owner Heather Leonard said she has been searching for since the shop outgrew its first home about two years after it opened.

The store, which specializes in pet nutrition and wellness and operates a dog bakery and raw bar, has moved to 212 N. Augusta Street in downtown Staunton. Leonard said the new location brings dedicated parking — something the original spot lacked — along with additional floor space for expanded shopping, services, and community events.

The reopening drew a crowd that included customers bringing dogs in need of homes, as well as vendors. Staff at the shop said they hope the larger footprint will let the business grow its community presence in the months ahead. The Well Balanced Paw is open Wednesday through Friday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Sunday noon to 5 p.m.

moreNews.headline: Staunton Hires New Public Works Director
moreNews.body: The City of Staunton named Brennen Duncan as its new Public Works Director, effective October 19. Duncan spent eleven years with the City of Charlottesville, where he most recently served as City Engineer. The announcement was posted to the city newsroom on October 8.

moreNews.headline: City Conducts Neighborhood Housing Conditions Survey
moreNews.body: On Saturday, October 24, the City of Staunton carried out a neighborhood housing survey in partnership with the Virginia Tech Center for Housing Research. Teams of volunteers, Virginia Tech students, and instructors walked and drove through designated neighborhoods to document exterior housing conditions — including roofs, porches, siding, windows, and doors — from public streets and sidewalks only. The city said individual properties will not be identified in any public reports and that the survey is unrelated to code enforcement or property tax assessments.

moreNews.headline: Missing Staunton Man Subject of State Police Alert
moreNews.body: Virginia State Police issued a Critically Missing Adult alert on October 30 for Jeffrey Scott Bennett, 56, of Staunton, whose disappearance poses a credible threat to his health and safety. Bennett was last seen at his Staunton home on October 29 at approximately 8:30 a.m. and is believed to be traveling near the Blue Ridge Parkway, possibly in a 1995 Toyota T100 pickup truck with Virginia plates XGG8878. Anyone with information should contact the Staunton Police Department.

hotels.name: Tru by Hilton Staunton

hotels.name: Fairfield by Marriott Inn & Suites Staunton
